title: finding(app-shell): the page designer writes page:tabs items[].key — a key PageTabsProps refuses by name and the tabs renderer never reads
body:
Found by the census objectui#8216 asked for (branch `claude/issue-8216-block-config-schema-parity`). Filed unassigned, out of that card's scope — objectui#8216 ships the gate and ledgers this key; the resolution is this card's.

Measured on `origin/main` `f20e57d62`, installed `@objectstack/spec` `17.2.0`.

## What

`BLOCK_CONFIG['page:tabs']` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/block-config.ts`) offers one array control, `items`, whose item editors are `key` and `label`. `PageBlockInspector.renderField` writes an item key VERBATIM — `next[i] = { ...itemObj, [n]: v }` — so an author who fills the first box gets `properties.items[0].key`.

Three faces disagree with that spelling:

- **The spec refuses it by name.** `ComponentPropsMap['page:tabs']` is strict, and its item shape declares `label`, `icon`, `visibleWhen`, `value`, `count`, `children`. Measured at runtime:
  `ComponentPropsMap['page:tabs'].safeParse({ items: [{ key: 'a', label: 'A' }] })` returns `success: false` with `unrecognized_keys` naming `key` at path `items.0`.
- **The renderer never reads it.** `PageTabsRenderer` (`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx:630`) builds `itemsWithValue` from `it.value`, falling back to an index-derived `tab-IDX` when absent. There is no read of `it.key` in that file.
- **The repo's own prose already says `value` is the live key.** `previews/__tests__/block-config.test.ts` states it inside the `page:accordion` describe: the accordion's panel id is unconditionally derived, "the tabs one is genuinely live", and `PageTabsProps.items[].value` "is a real, declared schema member". The designer control simply does not write that member.

## Consequence

A tab strip built in Studio carries no stable per-tab value, so every tab falls back to `tab-IDX`. That is exactly the failure objectui#2257 dealt with for the URL-addressable active tab (`?tab=`): an index value silently points at a different tab once the item list changes. The author DID supply a stable identifier; it landed under a key nothing reads.

The key additionally reaches the platform's component-props lint as an unknown authoring key: `PageComponent.properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` so the page parse itself stays green, and `ComponentPropsMap[type]` is reached only by the lint gate that dispatches on the sibling `type` (the spec's own note on `lintUnknownKeysAgainstSchema`, objectstack#5068).

## The decision this needs

Contract-first (AGENTS.md #0.1) points at the producer, and the producer is this table — the fix is to rename the control to `value`, not to teach the renderer a second spelling. But the rename is not a one-line edit and that is why it is a card rather than a rider:

- the field `name` is the i18n key's last segment, so `engine.inspector.pageBlock.field.page:tabs.items.key` becomes `...items.value` in BOTH locale tables in `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, and the retired key must leave both (the pattern objectui#3829 and objectui#5212 set);
- documents saved by every released build carry `items[].key`, so the read-door question objectui#7772 answered with `stripRetiredBlockProps` applies here too — except this one is a NESTED key, which that helper does not reach;
- objectui#3912 is open against the same box for a different reason (no pattern/validate affordance on `BlockPropField`), so whoever takes this should read that card first.

## Related
